description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994; the s491 write-up had it as "a pure-Perl core module the compiler refuses").  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  File::Copy 2.41 starts `use 5.035007;`, which is what arms it.

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/sig1.pl):
  use v5.36;
  sub f { my $ok = 1;
      if ($ok) {
          $ok = grep { $_ == 5 } split /\s+/, $)
      }
      return $ok; }
  say f() ? "yes" : "no";
  perl: no     PCL: three announced drops ("line 5: )", "line 6: }", "line 8: }") and the runtime dies at the first.
Without the pragma line: identical to perl.  With `$x` in place of `$)`: fine.  A semicolon after `$)` does NOT help (sig2.pl).  At FILE level `use v5.36; my $e = $); print ...` happens to work (no enclosing structure for the stray paren to close) -- so probe inside `if (...) {}`, `sub {}`, a call's argument list `f(1, $))`, `($(, $))`, a string `"$)"` (InterpScan owns that one -- probe it, do not assume), `$) =~ /\d/`, `split ' ', $)` and `$(` beside it (is `$(` hit too?  Unknown.pm has two `)` arms and one `%noname` arm).

THE TOKEN DUMP (PPI 1.291, `PPI::Document->new(FILE, feature_mods => { signatures => 1 })`, line 5):
  ... Word:split | Regexp::Match:/\s+/ | Operator:, | Symbol:$ | Structure:)          expected: ... | Magic:$)
CAUSE IN PPI: PPI/Token/Unknown.pm lines ~120, ~164, ~215 test `$t->_current_token_has_signatures_active` -- which is FILE-REGION state ("the feature is on"), not "the tokenizer is inside a signature" -- and turn `$` + `)` into an unnamed placeholder parameter + the closing paren.  Inside a real signature that is right (`sub f ($x, $) {...}`); anywhere else `$)` is the effective GID.

RULE 13 (same commit as the workaround): a section in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md (repro, dump, PPI version, the workaround and what it unblocks), a FAILING row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t (bump `tests => N`), a canary row in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.
THE WORKAROUND's shape: one token repair in the family `_ppi_parse` already runs (`_merge_punct_array_symbols` and friends; `Pl::Parser::fragment_doc` must run it too -- #435): a Symbol whose content is exactly `$` immediately followed (ADJACENT, no whitespace) by Structure `)` is re-merged into Magic `$)` UNLESS it sits in a signature (the enclosing structure is a `PPI::Structure::Signature`, or the PPI-version-appropriate test: the `)` closes the paren that directly follows `sub NAME` / `sub`).  BUT merging tokens is not enough when the LEXER has already closed the wrong structure with that `)` (the #410 lesson: PPI had built the following `{...}` as a BLOCK and the postfix chain had to be re-classed) -- so measure first whether a token-level repair can run BEFORE the lexer builds the tree (a custom tokenizer pass / re-lex of the repaired source text), and if not, whether rewriting the SOURCE TEXT before PPI sees it (`$)` -> `${)}` outside signatures, positions preserved?) is the smaller honest repair.  Say which you chose and why in ppi-upstream-bugs.md.

ACCEPTANCE: `use File::Copy; copy($a, $b); move(...); cp(...)` on temp files == perl (contents, return values, the permission-preserving `cp`), and the battery's `modules.pl` count moves.  After the lex repair File::Copy may hit the NEXT thing (line 19: `BEGIN { eval q{ use Time::HiRes qw( stat utime ) } };` -- must fail soft as in perl when Time::HiRes is absent, or succeed once #1992's shim exists; `stat`/`utime` there are Time::HiRes's builtin-named exports = #1870's mechanism).  File what remains, per cause.

BAR: `Pl/` token repair => corpus-diff (expect IDENTICAL: no corpus file has `$)` under signatures -- say so with the grep) + emission-ab over lib + the board; gate-SET scan both populations (a refusal stops firing); guard rows in an existing signatures/ppi-repair Pl/t file, INVERSE-verified.


=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED 4881dba2.  PPI 1.291 decides `$` + `)` from FILE-REGION state ("the
feature is on"), not from "the tokenizer is inside a signature", so once
`use v5.36` is in force the magic variable `$)` is split EVERYWHERE.  Core
File::Copy starts `use 5.035007;` and was REFUSED WHOLE.

THE LAYER, decided by measurement: the stray `)` reaches the LEXER and is used
to close a structure -- the reproducer comes back with BOTH blocks unclosed
(`{ ... ???`) and three Statement::UnmatchedBrace at document level -- so a
token-class repair in the `_merge_punct_array_symbols` family runs too late to
undo it (#410's lesson).  The two honest options were a source pre-pass and a
post-lex RE-PARENTING of the wrecked statements; the second is a hand-written
re-lex, so the first is the smaller one.

THE ORACLE IS PPI'S OWN TOKENIZER RUN WITHOUT THE FEATURE TRACKING, which is
what makes a source repair safe: it answers `Magic:$)` for the variable in
every position, and every FALSE-POSITIVE shape keeps its `$)` INSIDE another
token (a real signature is one Prototype token -- named, leading-placeholder
and anon alike; a dq string one Quote::Double; a comment one Comment; a pattern
one Regexp::Match).  So the repair set is "a Magic token whose content is `$)`"
with no signature or paren analysis at all.  The token stream concatenates to
the source, so the running length is each token's byte offset; the replacement
`$;` is the SAME LENGTH, so every later offset, line and column is
byte-identical, and the token is put back after the parse by the same walk.
It lives in `_ppi_new`, the one construction site, and `fragment_doc` goes
through it (#435's lesson).

RULE 13, same commit: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section 32 (repro, token dump,
tree dump, PPI version, workaround, what it unblocks), three rows in
docs/ppi-bug-report.t (78 -> 82) of which two FAIL on 1.291, and a canary in
Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.

File::Copy then hit `use builtin 'blessed';`, dropped as a pragma without
importing -> `p-import-builtins` / `p-unimport-builtins` (generic: perl ALIASES
each named builtin into the calling package; a `:5.NN` bundle means every
builtin this runtime has; an unimplemented name is skipped, not fatal).  They
target `*package*`, not `*pcl-current-package*` -- measured: the runtime
current package still says MAIN while a module's own `use` runs.

ACCEPTANCE: `use File::Copy; copy/cp/move` on temp files is byte-identical to
perl (7 rows incl. cp's permission preservation).  The 8th -- copy of a MISSING
source -- crashes on a DIFFERENT bug, FILED as #2013 (a forward `goto LABEL`
lowered two ways in one sub).  Guard: 6 rows in Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t
(26 -> 32); on a 268d7e00 extraction both `$)` rows FAIL and the four inverse
rows -- the dq string, both signature placeholders, and `$)` with no pragma --
pass (scratch/s492a/inverse-guards-base268.log).
subject: EVERYDAY (File::Copy -- copy/move/cp/mv): core File::Copy.pm is REFUSED WHOLE ("PCL: statement not supported at .../File/Copy.pm line 238: )") -- a NEW PPI 1.291 MIS-LEX: once the `signatures` feature is on (`use v5.36`, `use 5.035007`, `use feature 'signatures'`), PPI lexes the magic variable `$)` EVERYWHERE as Symbol `$` + Structure `)`, not only inside a signature, and the stray `)` wrecks the enclosing block structure
